newsitem.title: USA: Continental declines comment on merger.
newsitem.headline: Continental declines comment on merger.

text.p: A Continental Airlines Inc spokesman, citing company policy, on Wednesday declined comment on rumors the Houston-based carrier was in merger talks with Delta Air Lines.
"It is our policy not to comment on rumor and speculation in the marketplace," the spokesman said.

According to news reports, Continental and Delta are in preliminary merger talks that would create the nation's largest air carrier. The Wall Street Journal also reported 10 top Continental executives sold 1.16 million shares valued at more than $30.3 million in recent weeks.

In a memo sent to airline employees on Wednesday, Continental's two top executives said they exercised stock options for year-end tax and investment purposes, and would not have sold shares if a merger were imminent.

"We would obviously not have exercised stock options if we thought a merger was around the corner which would create a windfall for all stockholders," Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Gordon Bethune and President and Chief Operating Officer Greg Brenneman said.
In the memo, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters, the executives said the airline is constantly assessing options in the event of an industry consolidation.

"Should an industry consolidation occur, and we are not saying it will, Continental will only be involved in a manner which is fair to both our Continental co-workers and our shareholders," the executives said in the memo.
